meetTab.seriesSplitNote: This series has two finals, so the path to the final splits in two ({{meetTotal}} racers in the series). The series rank and the semi-final line are calculated among the racers heading for the same final as the six boats shown.
meetTab.seriesSplitNoteNoBorder: This series has two finals, so the path to the final splits in two ({{meetTotal}} racers in the series). The series rank is calculated among the racers heading for the same final as the six boats shown.
meetTab.seriesMixedNote: This meet has two finals, but this race mixes boats from both, so the meet rank is calculated across all {{total}} racers in the meet.
meetTab.rankSourceNote: The series rank is our own calculation. We drop from the ranking racers with a flying start (F) this series before qualifying ended (excluded from prizes) and racers who withdrew (they ran on earlier days but have no race that day).
meetTab.rankSourceNoteAfterPrelim: An F after qualifying does not remove a racer from the ranking, but a withdrawal after qualifying does (both the same as the official list). So even after qualifying, ranks below can move up when a racer withdraws.
meetTab.rankSourceNoteOfficial: The score rate and series rank come from the official score-rate list as of the end of qualifying, including its deductions, prize exclusions and mid-series withdrawals. During qualifying the official list is not published yet, so our own tally is used.
meetTab.sparkNote: For ST the dashed line is the racer's usual average; for the trial it is the venue-wide average trial time for that day (how heavy the water was; it can move by nearly 0.1s). Higher is faster, and above the dashed line means fast for that day's water. The large dot is the latest run. The vertical scale is stretched to this racer's own min-max for the series, so the size of the peaks cannot be compared between racers. We do not label it as improving or declining. The ST label is colored (pushing harder in green, holding back in red) only with 3 or more runs this series and a gap of 0.02 or more.
meetTab.compareTrendTitle: How the six have moved this series
meetTab.compareTrendNote: All six ran the same series on the same water, so they share one scale (the min-max across the six) and you can compare the heights of the lines across rows directly. The dashed line is the average of the six. Higher is faster; the large dot is the latest run.
meetTab.compareTrendRange: The horizontal axis is the date ({{from}}–{{to}}). On days with two races the dots are shifted left and right, and the line breaks on days the racer did not race. The last dot in each row is the racer's previous race.
meetTab.compareTrendRangeOneDay: The horizontal axis is the date ({{day}}). Racers with two races that day have their dots shifted left and right. The last dot in each row is the racer's previous race.
meetTab.compareTrendHint: Tap a row to switch the details below to that racer
meetTab.compareTrendFinishNote: The number under each dot is the finish in that race. Races without a finish show a mark (F = flying start, Abs = absent, Eng = engine stall, etc.; tap ? on the "Last race this series" row of the data table for the full list).

meetTab.forecastTitle: Score-rate outlook (how today's finish moves it)
meetTab.forecastNote: A highlighted cell means that, with that finish today, the racer should be at or above the semi-final line ({{slots}}th = {{rate}}) at the end of today. On days with more qualifying races tomorrow, it does not settle the semi-final. Racers with two or more qualifying races left today are not highlighted, because one finish alone does not decide it. "Points needed" is what it takes to reach that line, counting only today's carded qualifying races (it changes if there are more qualifying races tomorrow).
meetTab.forecastNoteNoBorder: The score rate you would have after that finish. Assumes a clean finish.
meetTab.forecastRateBlueNote: A blue score rate means the racer is at or above the semi-final line right now. It can drop with today's finish, so read it together with the points-needed column.
meetTab.forecastDetailSummary: How the line and the points needed are derived
meetTab.forecastDetail: The line is the score rate of the {{slots}}th racer when qualifying ended. It can differ from the real border by a few places (measured: 0.07 at Wakamatsu G1, 0.83 at a Kiryu general series — we do not use the official remarks during qualifying, so we cannot exclude racers who were excluded from prizes for reasons other than a flying start, and general series do not always pick semi-finalists purely by score rate). Points needed = line x (runs so far + remaining runs) - points so far, where remaining runs are the carded qualifying races for today (some racers run twice, so it differs per racer). It assumes a clean finish, and we never call it a lock.
meetTab.withdrawnTitle: Treated as having withdrawn (the racer ran on earlier days but has no race that day; our own estimate. The official table also drops mid-series withdrawals from the ranking)
meetTab.withdrawnOfficialTitle: Withdrew mid-series per the official score-rate list remarks (dropped from the ranking, as in the official table)
meetTab.awardExcludedTitle: Excluded from prizes per the official score table remarks (cannot ride the semi-final or final). Like the official table, we drop them from the ranking
meetTab.flyingExcludedTitle: Excluded from prizes after a flying start (F) this series (cannot ride the semi-final or final). Like the official table, we drop them from the ranking. Our own judgement (the official score-rate list is used after qualifying ends)

meetTab.absentNote: "Absent" marks a racer who has not started any race so far this series. With 0 starts, there is no score rate or series rank.

st.title: ⏱️ Exhibition vs Actual ST Gap
st.description: Select a race being held today to see how much each racer's exhibition ST has historically deviated from their actual race ST. The smaller the gap, the more "stable" the racer — their exhibition ST is a reliable reference.

techProfile.title: 🏆 Racer Winning Technique Profile

techProfile.note: 💡 The breakdown is the share within races that racer won in the past 90 days. For racers with few wins, the tendency is less reliable.

returnRate.title: 💰 Racer × Boat Number ROI
returnRate.description: Select a race being held today to see each racer's Win/Place bet return rate over the past 180 days when racing from the same boat number. A perspective on whether betting on them actually pays, beyond win rates.
returnRate.note: 💡 The return rate is the total payout ratio if you had kept placing ¥100 Win/Place bets on every race from the same boat number over the past 180 days. Note that a small sample size reduces reliability.

st.dataView: This calculates, from each racer's past results, how much the start timing typically differs between the exhibition start (exhibition ST) and the actual race (actual ST). The smaller the gap, the more "stable" the racer — their exhibition ST is a reliable reference.

tips.text: = their exhibition ST tends to be a reliable guide for the actual race
= may fall apart in the actual race even with a good exhibition, slightly lowering reliability
Click a table row to see that racer's gap trend across past races

st.articleLinkText: What is the Exhibition vs Actual ST Gap? A new feature to spot racers who are "fast in exhibition but slow off the actual start"

topstart.title: About Top Start Analysis by Lane
topstart.dataView: Based on race results from the past 90 days, this analyzes by lane, for each venue, "which lane tends to record the fastest start (top start rate)" and "how often a top start actually converts to a win (win rate after top start)."

tips.strong: Lanes with a high top start rate but low win rate
tips.text: = may tend to get out first but fail to win

tips.strong: Lanes with a high win rate after top start
tips.text: = tend to convert a fast start directly into a win
Each venue has different characteristics, so the tendency changes significantly depending on the venue you select

topstart.articleLinkText: What is Top Start Analysis by Lane? A new feature to spot lanes that merely "get out first"

losing.title: About Losing Technique Analysis
losing.dataView: Based on race results from the past 90 days, this analyzes by lane, for each venue, which technique (Nige, Sashi, Makuri, etc.) the winner used when that lane failed to finish first. It is the mirror image of Winning Technique Analysis, showing tendencies in how a lane loses.

tips.strong: Lanes with a high rate of losing to Sashi
tips.text: = tend to be passed from the inside, a weaker-holding tendency

tips.strong: Lanes with a high rate of losing to Makuri
tips.text: = tend to be weak against a charge from the outside
Seeing which technique tends to beat boat 1 helps predict how the race develops when Nige fails

losing.articleLinkText: What is Losing Technique Analysis? A new feature to spot a venue/lane's weaknesses from how it loses

nige.title: About Outcome Distribution After a Nige Win
nige.dataView: Based on race results from the past 90 days, this analyzes 2nd/3rd place appearance patterns limited to races won by "Nige" (wire-to-wire escape). Unlike Outcome Distribution (an overall tally regardless of technique), this shows tendencies specific to races decided by an escape.

tips.text: Lets you grasp which boats tend to finish 2nd/3rd when boat 1 wins by Nige
Cases where a boat other than boat 1 wins by Nige are rare and useful as a reference for upset-prone races
Comparing with the technique-agnostic Outcome Distribution lets you isolate the tendencies specific to Nige

nige.articleLinkText: What is Outcome Distribution After a Nige Win? A new feature to narrow down picks after an inside escape

extime.title: About Fastest Exhibition Time → Win Conversion
extime.dataView: Based on race results from the past 90 days, this analyzes by lane, for each venue, "which lane tends to record the fastest exhibition (lap) time" and "how often the fastest boat actually wins."

tips.strong: Lanes with a high fastest-exhibition rate but low win rate
tips.text: = may be fast in exhibition but unable to close out the race

tips.strong: Lanes with a high win rate when fastest
tips.text: = tend to convert exhibition speed directly into a win
Combine with the Exhibition vs Actual ST Gap analysis to judge exhibition reliability from multiple angles

extime.articleLinkText: What is Fastest Exhibition Time → Win Conversion? A new feature to spot the reliability of "fast in exhibition" boats

extrend.title: About Racer Exhibition Time Trend
extrend.dataView: This shows how each racer's exhibition (lap) time has trended over the past 90 days. Unlike Fastest Exhibition Time → Win Conversion (venue/lane-based), this tracks each racer's individual condition.

tips.strong: Racers whose exhibition time keeps worsening
tips.text: = may be losing form, slightly lowering reliability

tips.strong: Racers with a stable or improving exhibition time
tips.text: = may be in good shape both in motor and physical condition
Click a table row to drill down into that racer's exhibition time trend chart

extrend.articleLinkText: What is Racer Exhibition Time Trend? A new feature to read a racer's ups and downs from their exhibition time

techprofile.title: About Racer Winning Technique Profile
techprofile.dataView: This shows, as a percentage breakdown, which technique (Nige, Sashi, Makuri, etc.) each racer has used to win over the past 90 days. Unlike the venue/lane-based Winning Technique tab, this shows each racer's individual winning pattern.

tips.strong: Racers with a high Nige rate
tips.text: = the type who leads and escapes; tends to show strength from the inside lane

tips.strong: Racers with a high Makuri/Makuri-zashi rate
tips.text: = have the power to win even from an outer lane
For racers with few wins, the technique breakdown is less reliable — please keep this in mind

techprofile.articleLinkText: What is Racer Winning Technique Profile? A new feature to spot a racer's winning pattern

formranking.title: About Today's Hot & Cold Racers Ranking
formranking.dataView: For every racer running today, this compares their current national win rate with their rate from about 90 days ago and ranks the top 10 with the largest change (delta) in two lists: "Rising" and "Falling." Unlike other tabs, this lets you discover notable racers across today's entire card without selecting a venue or race.

tips.text: = recently in good form; can be used as grounds for a favorable pick
= recently in poor form; can be used as grounds for exclusion
Click a racer's name to see details in the Racer Form tab for their race today
Note that recently debuted rookies rise from a 0% win rate and easily appear in the rising ranking

formranking.articleLinkText: What is Today's Hot & Cold Racers Ranking? A new feature to discover notable racers without picking a race

returnrate.title: About Racer × Boat Number ROI Analysis
returnrate.dataView: For each racer, this shows the total payout ratio (return rate) from continuously placing ¥100 Win/Place bets on every race over the past 180 days where that racer raced from the same boat number. It does not use the AI prediction model's probabilities — only actual paid-out amounts are tallied.

tips.strong: Racers with a high return rate
tips.text: = tend to be profitable to actually bet on, not just have a high win rate
A racer with a high win rate but low return rate may be popular, with odds concentrated low (little value)
For racers with a small sample size, the return rate is less reliable — please keep this in mind

returnrate.articleLinkText: What is Racer × Boat Number ROI Analysis? A new feature to see profitability, not just win rate

attackdefense.title: About Advanced Race Data
attackdefense.dataView: For each racer, this shows the distribution of "how they have attacked and won" by lane (attack: Sashi, Makuri, Makuri-zashi, etc.) and, for lane 1 racers, "how they have been attacked and beaten" (defense). Comparing with the national average reveals a racer's attacking style.

tips.strong: Outer-lane racers with frequent Makuri attacks
tips.text: = can be a starting point for a high payout in races where the course 1 boat is weak on defense
The course 1 racer's defense distribution shows which technique tends to beat them
Combining this with the Winning Technique tab (venue/lane-based) or the Racer Winning Technique Profile tab builds up stronger grounds

racecard.title: About Race Card Data
racecard.dataView: This lists the six racers' class, win rate, motor, average ST, exhibition, and lane win rate in lane order. Colored values indicate the top 3 in the race. This is pure race card data, with no AI prediction score or sorting applied.

tips.text: = rank in the top 3 across multiple metrics in the race; strong overall on the data side
A racer with a fast average ST and high ST consistency tends to have an edge in the start
The Race Data Table on the race page is a summary of analysis indicators; this tab is the raw data listing

venueranking.title: About Venue Ranking
venueranking.dataView: Aggregates today's finished races by venue and ranks them by four indicators: average trifecta payout (stable/rough), boat 1's Nige success rate, and the big-payout (¥10,000+) occurrence rate. Also shows boat 1's win rate over the past 90 days across all 24 venues (this one indicator alone is a 90-day aggregate, not today-only).

tips.text: = boat 1's Nige tends to succeed here. Good picks for favorite-backers
= upsets tend to happen here. Good picks for longshot-hunters
Stable/rough/Nige rate/big-payout rate are real-time, today-only tallies; boat 1 win rate alone is a 90-day aggregate — keep them distinct when reading
The four today-only indicators are less reliable early in the day, when few races have finished

venuegrade.title: About Venue × Grade Analysis
venuegrade.dataView: For the selected venue, compares per-lane win rate, top-2 rate, and top-3 rate — or whole-race big-payout rate and average payout — across race grades (ippan/G3/G2/G1/SG). Cells backed by fewer than 50 races show "-".

tips.strong: A venue where lane 1 gets weaker as the grade rises
tips.text: = the patterns that work for ippan races may not carry over to SG/G1
SG/G2 are only held at a handful of venues, so seeing many "-" cells for those grades is normal, not a bug
The bigger the gap between a venue-grade combination and the national average, the more it should weigh into your bet selection

volatility.title: About the Upset Index Track Record
volatility.dataView: Shows the new AI model's (launched August 11, 2026) "upset index" — a within-venue percentile of how likely boat 1 is to be upset — broken down by level (warning/standard/stable) against actual outcomes.

tips.text: -labeled races tend to have a higher-than-average actual upset rate
-labeled races tend to have a lower-than-average actual upset rate
Since this model just launched, the sample size is still small and accuracy will improve as more data accumulates
This is the same metric shown as the "Upset Alert" badge on each race's prediction screen

weather.title: About wind and course-1 wins
weather.dataView: Using about 370,000 races from the official results (K files) since February 2020, we convert the wind at race time to the water's direction (tailwind = from Mark 2 toward Mark 1) and compare the course-1 win rate with the same venue's average. The comparison and pass criteria were fixed before looking at the results.

tips.text: lower the course-1 win rate at almost every venue
vary a lot by venue, so check your venue
The pre-race wind may be the previous race's value and can change before the start. Use it as a guide.

termHints.winRate: The racer's national win rate, the figure used for class ratings. Higher means a stronger racer
termHints.localWinRate: The racer's win rate at this venue. A guide to whether this is one of their strong venues
termHints.motor: The share of races this motor finished 1st or 2nd. A higher figure suggests a motor in good condition
termHints.form: The difference between the racer's recent win rate and their usual win rate, showing whether they are trending up or down
termHints.avgSt: Average start timing. Smaller means faster starts
termHints.st: How little the racer's start timing varies. Smaller means consistently steady starts
termHints.exSt: Start timing in the pre-race exhibition run
termHints.exhibition: Time in the pre-race exhibition run. Smaller suggests a stronger engine
termHints.oriLap: Seconds taken to complete one lap in the exhibition run. Smaller suggests better all-round speed
termHints.oriHalfLap: Seconds taken for half a lap (1st mark to 2nd mark) in the exhibition run. Smaller is better
termHints.oriTurn: Seconds taken through the turn in the exhibition run. Smaller means a sharper turn, making it easier to get ahead with Sashi (Inside pass) or Makuri-zashi (Sweep & pass)
termHints.oriStraight: Seconds on the straight section of the exhibition run. Smaller means better straight-line speed, helping Makuri (Outside sweep) and late charges
termHints.courseRate: Past win rate from this boat number (lane)
termHints.tilt: The motor's angle (tilt) setting, chosen by the racer for the exhibition. A higher or lower value does not by itself mean a good or poor run
termHints.adjustmentWeight: Ballast added to the boat to offset the racer's body weight. A higher or lower value does not by itself mean a good or poor run
termHints.todayWeight: The racer's weight measured on race day. A higher or lower value does not by itself mean a good or poor run
termHints.partsChanged: Parts or propellers replaced for this race. A replacement is not by itself good or bad
termHints.exhibitionCourse: The course the boat actually took in the start exhibition (the official pre-race value as published). Courses that differ from the boat number are colored and marked as moving inside (e.g. maezuke) or outside. The actual race entry may differ
termHints.entryCourseDistribution: How often the boat entered from each course in the race itself, across races where it started from the same boat number as today (since Dec 2025, up to the past 2 years). Wakunari = the course matching the boat number; maezuke = moving into a course inside the boat number. Bars are shown faded for boats with fewer than 6 races
termHints.exhibitionTopRate: 1st-place rate, top-2 rate and top-3 rate, limited to races where this boat had the outright fastest exhibition time (since Dec 2025, up to the past 2 years)
termHints.meetExhibitionTrend: The exhibition time from the previous race and the average exhibition time this meet (since the racer started using this motor)
termHints.meetOriLap: Exhibition full-lap time from the previous race this meet and the meet average. Available before this race's exhibition is published
termHints.meetOriHalfLap: Exhibition half-lap (1st mark to 2nd mark) time from the previous race this meet and the meet average. Available before this race's exhibition is published
termHints.meetOriTurn: Exhibition turn time from the previous race this meet and the meet average. Smaller means a sharper turn. Available before this race's exhibition is published
termHints.meetOriStraight: Exhibition straight-section time from the previous race this meet and the meet average. Smaller means better straight-line speed. Available before this race's exhibition is published
termHints.prevResult: Finish position and entry course from the racer's most recent race before this one at the same venue in the same meet (including races on previous days). The lower line shows that race's date and race number. If the racer has not raced yet this meet, it shows "First race of the event". Races without a finishing position are shown with a mark: F = flying start, L = late start, Abs = absent, Cap = capsized, Fell = fell overboard, Sank = sank, Obs = obstruction, Eng = engine stall, DNF = did not finish, DQ = disqualified, — = no position recorded. If the previous race's result is not in yet, it shows "Awaiting result" with that race's date and race number (results update hourly, so it may show "Awaiting result" for a while after the race ends)
termHints.technique: The racer's favorite winning style (Nige (Escape), Sashi (Inside pass), Makuri (Outside sweep), etc.). A clue for reading the turn prediction
termHints.returnRate: Past return rate if you had actually bet on this boat number (reference value only; not a guarantee of results)
termHints.turnPrediction: AI prediction of which boat is likely to win, and with which winning technique (Nige = escape, Sashi = inside pass, Makuri = outside sweep…), shown as the top patterns with probabilities. The technique is mostly decided at the first mark (1st turn)
termHints.inKuzureIndex: How likely Boat 1 (the inside course) is to lose, on a 0–100 scale compared with races at the same venue over the past 90 days (0 = most solid, 100 = most likely to be upset)
termHints.venueTendency: Past tendencies at this venue by boat number (course), such as winning techniques and win rates
termHints.venueTendencyTechnique: The winning techniques (Nige (Escape), Sashi (Inside pass), Makuri (Outside sweep), etc.) this boat number has used when it won
termHints.venueTendencyTopStart: How often this boat number made the fastest start (top start)
termHints.venueTendencyLosing: When this boat number lost, which of the opponent's winning techniques it most often lost to
termHints.venueTendencyExhibitionTop: How often the boat with the fastest exhibition time went on to finish 1st
termHints.motorCondition: Chart of each motor's recent condition at this venue (win rate trend)
termHints.racerForm: Chart of each racer's recent results trend (win rate going up or down)
termHints.stDeviation: Analysis of each racer's start timing variation and consistency
termHints.exhibitionTimeTrend: Chart of recent exhibition times. Smaller suggests a stronger engine
termHints.racerTechniqueProfile: Which winning techniques (Nige (Escape), Sashi (Inside pass), Makuri (Outside sweep), etc.) each racer has won with in the past
termHints.returnRateAnalysis: Return rate data based on past results. Reference values only; not a guarantee of results
termHints.attackDefense: Detailed analysis of past race development (attack and defense patterns by course)
termHints.pitConfidence: Shown exactly as it appears on the official site. The official site does not define what the ★ marks mean
termHints.stStable: The share of starts within 0.05 seconds of the fastest starter in that race. Shows whether the racer keeps pace at the start. Flying starts are excluded. This is our own aggregation and will not match similarly named stats on other sites
termHints.stBreakout: The number of times the racer started at least 0.07 seconds ahead of every boat on an inner course. Shows whether they can attack the inside from an outer course. This happens less often the further out the course (0.2–0.4 times per 30 races from courses 5 and 6), and as a percentage it would mostly read 0.0%, so we show a count. "Average" is the break rate of racers on the same course and class multiplied by this racer's number of races (how many times an average racer would do it in as many races). Not shown for course 1, which has no boat inside it. Flying starts are excluded. This is our own aggregation and will not match similarly named stats on other sites
termHints.stLate: The share of starts 0.1 seconds or more behind the fastest starter in that race. Because this tends to rise on outer courses, the gap from the average for the same course and class is shown too. Flying starts are excluded. This is our own aggregation and will not match similarly named stats on other sites
termHints.flyingCount: Class is the value on this race's program. F is the number of flying starts this term (gold = 1, red = 2) and resets to 0 on May 1 and November 1. A "this meet" tag means the racer had a flying start between the first day of this meet and yesterday: they still run the rest of the meet but cannot enter this meet's semifinal or final (excluded from prizes; today's F is not counted). L is the number of late starts, which is different from "Slow" below. Consistent and Slow exclude races with a flying start
termHints.nigeSimulation: Using only races where the course 1 boat won by Nige (Escape), the share of each course that finished 2nd. This is aggregated from this venue's actual results, not a prediction
